data.body:
UPSTREAM DECISION RESOLVED — set_reporter. The plan offered a binary (teach the call site DC's name
identity, OR declare reporter sync unsupported). Both were wrong. The evidence gives a three-part
answer, and one part is a defect neither the plan nor the reviewer had.

(1) THE CALL SITE NEEDS NO CHANGE — my own J7 fix already did that work.
    jira_account_id (identity.py:224) resolves an identity and returns its {provider:'jira'}
    external_id. Since [rebar:5f48-244c-7063-42d0] merged, DC ghost identities are minted under
    provider 'jira' with external_id = the DC USERNAME. Measured on a scratch repo after minting a DC
    identity:
        jira_account_id('1bb8-9d6a-dee5-46b5') -> 'dcuser'     # identity TICKET ID
        jira_account_id('dcuser')              -> None          # bare username
        jira_account_id('DC User')             -> None          # display name
        jira_account_id('dcuser@example.com')  -> None          # email
    So the seam is already vendor-neutral: it hands back whatever external_id the FAMILY stored, which
    for DC is the username — exactly the value DC's REST needs. set_reporter is therefore NOT
    unreachable; it is CONDITIONALLY reachable, on tickets whose reporter field holds an identity id.
    The reviewer's 'unreachable' verdict was correct for the tree it read; the merged J7 fix changed
    it underneath. dispatch_apply_phases.py comes OFF the scope list.

(2) THE TRANSPORT METHOD IS NEEDED, with a DC payload. Cloud PUTs reporter.accountId; DC has no
    accountId at all, so DC must PUT {'fields': {'reporter': {'name': <username>}}}. Note the local
    variable is called account_id at the call site and will hold a USERNAME on DC — functionally
    correct, misleadingly named.

(3) THE DEFECT NEITHER OF US HAD: reporter would CHURN FOREVER on DC, never converging.
    inbound_fields._identity_of (:163) builds the canonical identity as
        'account_id': raw.get('accountId')
    reading ONLY accountId. Measured against the two real reporter shapes:
        Cloud {'accountId': '557058:abc', ...} -> {'display':'Cloud User','email':'c@x.com','account_id':'557058:abc'}
        DC    {'name':'dcuser', ...}           -> {'display':'DC User','email':'d@x.com','account_id':None}
    So on DC remote_acct is ALWAYS None. outbound_field_diff._diff_reporter (:105-111) then computes
    'desired' from the local reporter and emits changed['reporter'] whenever desired != remote_acct.
    For any RESOLVABLE reporter that comparison can never match, so the mutation is re-emitted on
    EVERY pass — even immediately after set_reporter succeeds, because the next snapshot still yields
    account_id=None. This is the same pathology as the pre-8b25 parent bug documented in
    dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent (~230 steady-state mutations of perpetual re-emission).

    That directly breaks THIS STORY'S OWN AC: 'an immediately repeated writing pass writes nothing
    (idempotence)'. So implementing set_reporter WITHOUT fixing _identity_of would turn a currently
    silent no-op into visible infinite churn — strictly worse, and it would fail the live idempotence
    test. _identity_of must also read DC's 'name' into the canonical identity.

VERDICT for the plan: set_reporter -> IMPLEMENT (DC {'name': ...} payload) + fix
inbound_fields._identity_of to carry DC's name, NO change to dispatch_apply_phases.py.
That is the third time this epic has produced the same shape: the obvious half-fix converts a silent
failure into a louder one without making the capability work.
